thread:
Mira: quick heads-up — canary ran into OOM on a 32GB A100 when prefetch + rendezvous path hit a large KV-heavy chat. repro attached, short log below :eyes:

Sam: ugh, when did this start? regression from last week?

Mira: looks like after the batch-formation tweak that increased early prefetch. last successful canary was 4311200000, this started 4312300000-ish. low-hanging logs:
```
[2026-03-10T14:12:03Z] batch_builder.cc:285 build_batch(): reserved_tokens=4096, prefetch_reserve=6144, kv_mem_before=18.3GB, kv_mem_after=33.1GB --> OOM
[2026-03-10T14:12:03Z] kernel_selector.cc:142 select_kernel(): chosen=mixed-fast, fallback=quantized-fallback
[2026-03-10T14:12:03Z] oom_guard.cc:58 triggered_by=batch_prefetch
```

Kai: hm that log is useful. two quick notes: 1) prefetch_reserve of 1.5x token budget was an experiment; 2) the rendezvous path currently does prefetching without checking current KV footprint epoch, so it doesn't respect soft-headroom.

Jena: is kernel fallback exacerbating this? mixed-fast chooses a kernel path that needs a larger KV staging area, right?

Ryan: yes — mixed-fast allocates temporary KV scratch per request to speed attention splits. profiling snippet (hot paths):
```
allocs: KV staging 42%, KV metadata 18%, batch assembly overhead 12%, kernel temp 20%
peak_mem_by_component: kv_cache=19.8GB, staging=6.2GB, kernel_temp=4.7GB
```
if staging is unbounded during batch build we can overshoot 32GB easily.

Sam: short-term mitigation idea: 1) clamp prefetch multiplier to 1.0 if kv_cache > 14GB, 2) reduce batch-window from 7ms -> 3ms on A100-32 during canary, 3) force kernel selection to fallback that uses streaming kernels (less temp memory) when soft_headroom < 3GB.

Mira: I can run a canary with those knobs. what about long-term: we should teach the batch admission to consult KV footprints from the eviction tracker at admission time rather than only at commit. That lets us avoid admitting batches that will force prefetch into OOM range.

Kai: agree. also want to add a tiny heuristic: when rendezvous sees a request with kv_prefetch_hint set, it should convert that hint into a token_budget cap proportional to remaining KV headroom: token_budget = min(request_budget, floor((soft_headroom - kernel_temp_guess)/avg_token_kv_cost)).

Jena: good, but we need to be careful computing avg_token_kv_cost — it varies by model length and quantization. we can use recent mmapped stats per-model to estimate.

Ryan: I ran a small simulation with current numbers, results: lowering prefetch multiplier from 1.5 -> 1.0 reduces peak mem by ~25% on heavy KV traces, latency impact < 4% p95 for short chats. attaching sim output snippet:
```
sim: trace=kv-heavy-20260303, prefetch_mult=1.5 -> peak 35.1GB, prefetch_mult=1.0 -> peak 26.4GB
latency_p95_change: +3.4%
```

Sam: 👍 let's do that immediate knob for canary and also schedule an eng-runtime design sync for the admission+kv-eviction integration. @Kai can you draft a short design doc?

Kai: on it. will add cost models and the token_budget formula.

Mira: I'll kick the canary now with these three temporary knobs and report back in ~30m. thanks all :rocket:

deploy-bot: Canary started: r=canary/kv-prefetch-clamp-2026-03-10 id=ci-98321 link: https://ci.internal/runs/98321

Mira: canary updated — initial results look good, no OOM so far, p95 latency +2.9%. saving logs to /artifacts/canary-98321.log

Sam: great, if canary holds we should roll this as a hotfix and then schedule the more invasive admission change.

Kai: will draft doc by EOD.

Mira: thanks, closing for now. will open a follow-up thread for the design PR.
